info.bio: Kim Fowley (born 27 July 1939, died 15 January 2015 aged 75) was a male American record producer, impresario, songwriter and sometime recording artist. The son of Hollywood character actor Douglas Fowley ( Singin' In The Rain ), Kim's scattergun career in the music industry was as varied and eccentric as it was long. He generally remained on the fringes of the mainstream industry, free to immerse himself in obscure and offbeat projects while occasionally stumbling on (and then happily milking) commercial success. scenes.name: Los primeros discos de ácido
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: «The Third Eye» de los Dovers (abril de 1966) es uno de los primeros intentos de reproducir el viaje de LSD en un disco y de los más exactos: fanfarria oriental, drones a lo Ravi Shankar, doce cuerdas de raga, melodía horizontal sin cambios de acorde, voz de «místico punk» y una espiral casi fuera de control. Dura 135 segundos pero condensa una experiencia de ocho horas. Grupo de instituto de Santa Bárbara que había hecho folk rock en Gold Star, se rehízo a comienzos de 1966 animado a «viajar por el bien de la banda»; el guitarrista Bruce Clawson tradujo su asombro y su terror en un formato pop. El título viene del best seller de Lobsang Rampa (en realidad Cyril Hoskin, de Devon), que también usaron Dylan y los 13th Floor Elevators de Austin, formados expresamente para difundir la conciencia LSD. Aquellos primeros discos de ácido no eran beatíficos sino crudos, salvajes y amenazantes: «The Trip» de Kim Fowley, «Ain’t It Hard» de los Gypsy Trips, «Free Advice» de The Great!! Society!!. Sin una gran discográfica detrás, «The Third Eye» cayó en el vacío, y Clawson oyó «Eight Miles High» en la radio unas semanas después.

scenes.name: Carreras en solitario: cantautores de finales de los sesenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los excéntricos de Los Ángeles (David Axelrod, cuyos breakbeats orquestales anticipan el trip-hop; Van Dyke Parks y su música de cámara pop; David Ackles, Kim Fowley, Wild Man Fischer) y los herederos del Greenwich (Laura Nyro, Eric Andersen, David Peel, Angus MacLise y Nico, cuyas letanías fúnebres inventan el rock gótico casi por accidente: Marble Index, Desert Shore). Canadá aporta a Leonard Cohen, Gordon Lightfoot, Joni Mitchell (Blue, Hejira) y Neil Young, que con Dylan y Springsteen forma la gran tríada «moral» de la música americana e inventa la guitarra distorsionada que influirá en el grunge. En Texas, Townes Van Zandt; en Gran Bretaña, Scott Walker, Nick Drake (Pink Moon), Roy Harper, John Martyn, Cat Stevens, Rod Stewart, Eric Burdon y Jack Bruce.

podcast.title: Accused of Credit Theft
podcast.body: Richie Polador accused Kim Fowley, along with Bruce Johnston and Sandy Nelson, of having "no scruples whatsoever" and taking credit for songs like "Geronimo" and "Charge" that Polador claimed he wrote and recorded in his own studio. "There are three guys in the business who really have no scruples whatsoever. They are Bruce Johnston, Kim Fowley and Sandy Nelson, and I was Mr Scruples."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: American International Pictures Work
podcast.body: Fowley undertook work for American International Pictures, where he was tasked with developing an instrumental piece for the film "Ghost of Drag Strip Hollow." "Kim Fowley was by this point doing some work for American International Pictures, and was asked to come up with an instrumental for a film called Ghost of Drag Strip Hollow."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Arrest and Army Enlistment
podcast.body: Fowley claimed he was arrested for stealing wine from a liquor store with an older accomplice and selling it to students. He was given a choice between joining the army or going to prison, opting for the army under the same deal as Dean Torrance, with whom he shared some training. "According to him, for stealing wine from a liquor store on Biagulf and who was twice his age, and selling it to other students at the school."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Denial of Involvement with The Gamblers
podcast.body: Despite Nick Renee's claim of his involvement, Kim Fowley explicitly denied any participation in The Gamblers' record. This is a rare instance, as Fowley is known for claiming involvement in almost every record. "Meanwhile Fowley says he was not involved at all, and given that this is about the only record in the history of the world that Fowley has ever said he wasn't on, I tend to believe him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Role as Roadie for The Flips
podcast.body: Kim Fowley served as a roadie and general hanger-on for Kip Tyler and The Flips, and was instrumental in connecting members of The Sleepwalkers (Bruce Johnston, Dave Shostack, Sandy Nelson) to The Flips when their original instrumentalists departed. "Kim Fowley was by this point a roadie and general hangar on for The Flips."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: University High School Party Organizer
podcast.body: Kim Fowley organized parties for University High School students, which he later claimed were his primary source of income. He admitted to hiring sex workers to occupy students from wealthy homes, then breaking into their houses to rearrange furniture for dancing. He also facilitated dope dealers at these parties for a cut and had friends steal from partygoers' cars. "Crowley claimed in later years that these parties were his major source of income, that he would hire sex workers to take fellow university high students who have big houses, off to a motel to have sex with them."

xref.title: Formation and Inspiration (1975)
xref.body: The Runaways were formed by producer Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the success of the all-female band Fanny. Active from 1975 to 1979, they are arguably recognized as the first all-female hard rock band, featuring future stars Joan Jett and Lita Ford. "The first is to a weirdo producer named Kim Fowley, who was inspired by the group to form the Runaways, arguably the first all-female hard rock band."

xref.title: Kim Fowley's Training Method
xref.body: Kim Fowley, the manager of The Runaways, prepared the band for live performances by having road crew members throw various items like bottles and paper at them during rehearsals. This method was intended to familiarize the band with the challenging reactions they might face on stage. "Kim Fowley, who was the manager of the runaways, actually prepared the band for playing live by having the road crew throw junk at them, bottles, paper, whatever, while they were rehearsing, just so they knew what they were getting into."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sexism and Abusive Rehearsal Tactics
xref.body: The band faced tremendous sexism throughout their career. Producer Kim Fowley was rumored to have had crew members throw objects at them during rehearsals, purportedly to accustom them to the abuse they would encounter during live performances. "Legend has it that Fowley had their crew throw stuff at them during rehearsals, so they get used to the abuse whenever they played live."
